hero.subtitle: VST3/AU sampler plugin built from scratch in JUCE. Granular synthesis, hand-coded tremolo DSP, and full DAW automation. Thesis project that became a real tool I actually use.

features.title: What It Does
features.subtitle: Built from scratch. Every feature solves a real problem I had while making music.

f1.title: Drag & Drop Loading
f1.desc: Drop any audio file into the plugin window. Instant waveform visualization so you know exactly what you're working with. Supports WAV, AIFF, MP3—basically anything JUCE can read.

f2.title: Granular Synthesis
f2.desc: Takes tiny slices of audio (grains) and plays them back with randomization. Great for ambient textures and weird sound design. Grain size, position randomization, and crossfade smoothing are all adjustable in real-time.

f3.title: Custom Tremolo Effect
f3.desc: Wrote this DSP from scratch—per-sample sine LFO for smooth amplitude modulation. Sounds way better than just automating volume. Independent rate and depth controls respond instantly.

f4.title: Filter System
f4.desc: High-pass and low-pass TPT filters from JUCE DSP. Zero-delay design means they respond instantly without artifacts. Full 20Hz-20kHz range—cut the lows, cut the highs, whatever the track needs.

f5.title: Built-in Compressor
f5.desc: JUCE's compressor module with full parameter control. Threshold, ratio, attack, release—all automatable. Useful for taming dynamics when you're layering granular textures.

f6.title: Tempo Control
f6.desc: Speed up or slow down samples from 20-300 BPM using ResamplingAudioSource. Extreme time-stretching creates interesting artifacts. Custom loop regions let you isolate specific sections for granular playback.

f7.title: Dual Waveform Display
f7.desc: Two waveform views—one shows the original file, one shows what's actually coming out after all the processing. Helpful for understanding what granular mode and tempo changes are actually doing to your sound.

f8.title: Volume Safety System
f8.desc: Automatically stops playback if peaks go over safe levels. Learned this the hard way during testing—saved my headphones more than once. No accidental ear damage from feedback loops or hot signals.

f9.title: Full DAW Automation
f9.desc: Every single parameter is automatable in your DAW. Built with AudioProcessorValueTreeState so session state is always saved. Set a parameter, save your project, reopen it—everything's exactly where you left it.

apvts.title: AudioProcessorValueTreeState
apvts.subtitle: Parameter management system for automation and state persistence

what.title: What It Does
what.desc: Manages all plugin parameters and handles DAW automation. Saves session state between sessions.

how.title: How It Works
how.desc: Each parameter gets a range and default value. The DAW reads and automates them automatically.

why.title: Why This Approach
why.desc: JUCE handles threading and state management internally. No manual code required for automation.

result.title: Result
result.desc: All parameters automatable without extra code.

code.title: PluginProcessor.cpp — Parameter Definition
code.what: Creates and returns plugin parameters with ranges and defaults.
code.how: Each AudioParameterFloat is added to a vector and converted to ParameterLayout.
code.why: Single definition point keeps parameters consistent. All parameters are automatable by default.

gain.title: Gain Parameter
gain.text: Controls output volume. Range 0.0-3.1623 (~+10dB) allows both attenuation and amplification.

tempo.title: Tempo Parameter
tempo.text: Controls playback speed via resampling. 20-300 BPM range enables extreme time-stretching effects.

filters.title: Filter Parameters
filters.text: Low-pass and high-pass filter cutoff frequencies. 20Hz-20kHz range for complete tonal control.

what.title: What It Does
what.desc: Main audio callback invoked by the DAW. Processes audio buffers in real-time with minimal latency.

how.title: How It Works
how.desc: Fetches audio from the file player, then applies filters → compressor → tremolo sequentially. Reads parameters from APVTS.

why.title: Why This Approach
why.desc: The audio thread has strict timing requirements. APVTS provides lock-free parameter access without blocking.

result.title: Result
result.desc: Low-latency processing with correct effect order. No audio dropouts during parameter changes.

code.title: PluginProcessor.cpp — Audio Processing
code.what: Applies all effects to incoming audio buffers.
code.how: Reads APVTS parameters, fetches audio, applies DSP sequentially, then applies final gain.
code.why: Sequential processing maintains correct effect order. JUCE DSP provides SIMD optimization.

safety.title: Volume Safety
safety.text: Automatically stops playback when dangerous levels are detected. Protects speakers and hearing.

params.title: Parameter Reading
params.text: APVTS provides thread-safe access through atomic pointers. Lock-free operation for the audio thread.

tempo.title: Tempo Control
tempo.text: Calculates the resampling ratio based on BPM. AudioFilePlayer uses ResamplingAudioSource for speed adjustments.

fetch.title: Audio Fetching
fetch.text: AudioFilePlayer fills the buffer with samples from the loaded file. Handles both looping and granular modes.

filterConfig.title: Filter Configuration
filterConfig.text: State Variable TPT filters respond instantly to cutoff changes without artifacts. Cutoffs are updated before processing each buffer.

dsp.title: DSP Processing
dsp.text: AudioBlock and ProcessContext enable SIMD optimization. In-place processing maximizes performance.

what.title: What It Does
what.desc: Amplitude modulation using a low-frequency oscillator. Creates rhythmic pulsing effects.

how.title: How It Works
how.desc: Sine wave LFO is calculated for each sample. Each sample is multiplied by the LFO value based on the depth parameter.

why.title: Why Custom Implementation
why.desc: Hand-coded for complete control over the effect. Per-sample processing ensures smooth modulation.

result.title: Result
result.desc: Smooth tremolo with precise rate and depth control. No aliasing or stepping artifacts.

code.title: PluginProcessor.cpp — Tremolo Implementation
code.what: Custom tremolo using sine wave LFO for amplitude modulation.
code.how: Phase increment is calculated per sample. Sine wave is applied to all channels.
code.why: Per-sample processing ensures smoothness. Manual implementation allows precise control.

phase.title: Phase Increment
phase.text: Converts Hz to radians per sample for sine generation. Ensures the LFO completes one cycle at the specified rate.

lfo.title: LFO Generation
lfo.text: Sine wave ranges from 0 to 1. Formula (1-depth)+(depth*LFO) ensures depth=0 produces no modulation.

processing.title: Per-Sample Processing
processing.text: Applies modulation across all channels. Direct buffer access maximizes performance.

wrap.title: Phase Wrapping
wrap.text: Wraps phase to prevent overflow. Keeps the value in the 0-2π range for continuous sine generation.

what.title: What's Used
what.desc: Built with JUCE's StateVariableTPTFilter and Compressor modules. Both are SIMD-optimized.

how.title: How They Work
how.desc: TPT filters use Topology-Preserving Transform for zero-delay filtering. Compressor uses look-ahead with smooth envelopes.

why.title: Why JUCE DSP
why.desc: JUCE DSP modules are already optimized and battle-tested. Saves development time while guaranteeing quality.

result.title: Result
result.desc: Professional-grade filtering and compression with low CPU usage. Parameters respond smoothly to changes.

code.title: PluginProcessor.cpp — DSP Setup
code.what: Initialization in prepareToPlay, called before audio processing starts.
code.how: ProcessSpec defines sample rate, block size, and channel count. All modules are prepared with the same spec.
code.why: prepareToPlay is called before processing begins. DSP modules need the correct sample rate and buffer sizes.

spec.title: ProcessSpec Configuration
spec.text: Defines the audio processing environment. All JUCE DSP modules require this spec to ensure consistent sample rate.

filterInit.title: Filter Initialization
filterInit.text: StateVariableTPTFilter provides zero-delay filtering through TPT design. Prepared and reset for clean startup.

compInit.title: Compressor Initialization
compInit.text: JUCE Compressor handles dynamic range control. Prepared with the same spec for proper operation.

audioPlayer.title: AudioFilePlayer System
audioPlayer.subtitle: File loading, playback, and tempo manipulation

what.title: What It Handles
what.desc: Manages file loading, playback, looping, and tempo control. Built with AudioTransportSource and ResamplingAudioSource.

how.title: How It's Built
how.desc: Files load into AudioFormatReaderSource, wrapped in ResamplingAudioSource, then connected to AudioTransportSource.

why.title: Why This Architecture
why.desc: JUCE's AudioSource architecture maintains clean separation. Each source handles a single responsibility.

result.title: Result
result.desc: Smooth playback with 20-300 BPM tempo control. Reliable looping and granular mode support.

code.title: AudioFilePlayer.cpp — Playback System
code.what: AudioSource chain for playback with tempo control.
code.how: Reader is wrapped in ResamplingAudioSource and connected to AudioTransportSource.
code.why: ResamplingAudioSource changes speed while maintaining quality. AudioTransportSource provides play/stop/loop functionality.

reading.title: File Reading
reading.text: AudioFormatManager detects the file format and creates the appropriate reader. Supports WAV, AIFF, MP3, and more.

resampling.title: Resampling Setup
resampling.text: ResamplingAudioSource enables tempo control. Ratio of 1.0 is normal speed, 2.0 is double speed.

transport.title: Transport Setup
transport.text: AudioTransportSource provides play/stop/loop controls. Manages playback position and handles looping automatically.

tempoControl.title: Tempo Control
tempoControl.text: Resampling ratio changes playback speed. Calculated from BPM: ratio = desiredBPM / 120.
